items.title: Royal Enfield Classic 350 Spied With Tubeless Spoke Wheels – Launch Soon
items.summary: A Classic 350 in Medallion Bronze has spied at at dealership with a different spoke-wheel setup - finally getting tubeless option on best selling RE
items.text: After years of waiting, Royal Enfield could finally launch the much awaited practical update for the Classic 350, with spyshots from dealership showing the motorcycle equipped with what appears to be a tubeless-compatible spoke wheel. The Medallion Bronze Classic 350 retains its familiar retro design, but a closer look at the front wheel reveals a different rim and spoke attachment arrangement. The close-up images show a black-finished front rim with spokes attaching to a raised flange. This differs from the conventional arrangement in which spoke pass through the central section of the rim. The visible construction appears consistent with a design intended to accommodate tubeless tyres. The motorcycle otherwise retains familiar components, including its telescopic front fork, front disc brake with ByBre caliper and ABS sensor ring. The wheel design appears to resemble the tubeless spoke-wheel setup associated with the Meteor 350 Sundowner Edition, rather than the side-laced arrangement seen on the Goan Classic 350. For Classic buyers who prefer the appearance of spokes, such an option could remove one reason to choose alloy wheels. The main attraction is puncture-repair convenience. Many small tread punctures in a tubeless tyre can be temporarily plugged without removing the wheel, making roadside repairs more manageable. items.title: Upcoming Hero Karizma XMR 250 spotted
items.summary: The Hero Karizma XMR 250 has been spotted at a dealership in a new red colour scheme. Tap here for more details.
items.text: The upcoming Hero Karizma XMR 250 has been spotted at a dealership in a red colour scheme. This isn’t the first time the bike has been seen in production form. Back in July, the model was spotted in a black colourway, following its initial showcase in white at EICMA 2024. In terms of overall design, the XMR 250 looks much like the XMR 210, with a similar projector LED headlamp and boomerang-shaped daytime running lights (DRLs). The fairing extends lower below the headlamp, and the bike gets integrated winglets. Also visible are a tall windscreen, a gold-finished USD fork, a sculpted fuel tank and a split seat. The Karizma XMR 250 will likely be powered by the same 249cc single-cylinder liquid-cooled engine as the Xtreme 250R, producing 30hp at 9,250rpm and 25.3Nm at 7,500rpm. This engine is paired with a 6-speed gearbox. Hero is yet to announce an official launch date or pricing for the Karizma XMR 250. However, the appearance of a production-ready motorcycle at a dealership suggests that a launch could be close. For reference, the Karizma XMR 210 is priced from Rs 1.86 lakh, while the Xtreme 250R is priced at Rs 1.84 lakh. The XMR 250 is expected to be priced above both models, close to the Rs 2 lakh mark. Its rivals will include the Suzuki Gixxer SF 250, KTM RC 200 and Yamaha R2.

items.title: Upcoming 2027 Honda CBR1000RR-R Spotted Testing
items.summary: The upcoming 2027 Honda CBR1000RR has been spotted testing abroad. The bike has undergone some important changes, including the addition of new brake calipers and some improvements to its aero.
items.text: Honda has started testing the upcoming 2027 CBR1000RR-R abroad, at the Jerez Circuit in Spain. It was ridden by Jonathan Rea, and images of the motorcycle were shared on his social media profile. The bike being tested right after the last round of the 2026 WorldSBK signals that the brand has some big plans for the 2027 WorldSBK. The bike has seen some changes, with the aeros being revised. At the front, the winglets have been enlarged for better downforce. In addition to this, the brand has also added ground effect pods, likely inspired by the Ducati Panigale V4 . These pods should improve the bike’s cornering speed, thus helping to improve lap times. Another interesting change is that the test mule was spotted with a differently shaped ram air intake compared to the current WorldSBK CBR1000RR-R. The reworked ram-air intake could have resulted in an improvement in performance. For reference, the current CBR1000RR-R is powered by a 999cc, liquid-cooled, inline-four engine that produces 217.5bhp at 14,000rpm and 113Nm at 12,000rpm. With the changes in regulations, we can expect the bike’s chassis to have received some tweaks. However, it is not clearly visible just going by the images shared online. Lastly, the brakes have been changed, with the test mule sporting Brembo callipers instead of the Nissin callipers. The change is likely due to Brembo being the new exclusive supplier of braking hardware for 2027 WorldSBK.

items.title: Jawa Yezdi and BSA Expand Spare-Parts Network to Ease Ownership
items.summary: All three brands now get a wider access to genuine spare parts beyond dealerships to improve repair times and make ownership easier across smaller cities.
items.text: Jawa Yezdi and BSA Motorcycles are expanding their genuine spare-parts distribution network across India allowing customers, independent workshops and service partners to source authorised components beyond the companies’ regular dealership channels. The initiative is being rolled out through authorised distribution partners at multiple strategic locations across the country. The strategy will improve parts procurement, increase availability and shorten service turnaround times across urban, semi-urban and emerging markets. This should mean owners no longer need to wait for a dealership to order and receive relatively routine replacement components before work can begin. This is more useful for smaller cities as spare-parts distribution can cover a much wider area without requiring the investment involved in opening complete sales and service facilities. This gives Jawa Yezdi an easier way to support owners in markets where volumes may not yet justify a full dealership.

items.summary: Moto Guzzi has announced the unveiling date for the Trip 500 retro roadster, based on the Aprilia 457 platform. The bike has been spotted testing multiple times abroad earlier. It could also be showcased at EICMA 2026.
items.text: Moto Guzzi has announced the unveiling date for the upcoming Trip 500 retro roadster. The brand shared the announcement via social media, and the upcoming bike will be revealed on 28 October 2026. It could also be showcased at EICMA 2027. The motorcycle’s name was previously revealed in patent filings, and now, with the social media announcement, we have official confirmation. The motorcycle will be based on the Aprilia 457 platform, but with some changes made to its design and underpinnings. From the images, we can see that the motorcycle has a round LED headlight setup, with the Moto Guzzi logo. It also features a muscular tank, but no tank extensions like the Tuono 457. The bike will use the same 457cc, parallel-twin, liquid-cooled engine as the Tuono 457 and the Aprilia RS 457 . The motor produces 47.6bhp and 43.5Nm on the Aprilia Tuono 457 . But Moto Guzzi could go with a different state of tune to suit the retro roadster’s character. The underpinnings have been slightly revised, with the rear suspension- an offset single-shock absorber- mounted on the swingarm. The revised suspension should result in slightly altered handling dynamics compared to the Tuono 457. So far, it is too early to tell if this upcoming retro roadster will come to India or not.

items.title: Centre Allows E100 Ethanol Fuel For Compatible Flex-Fuel Vehicles
items.summary: The Centre has approved E100 ethanol fuel for compatible flex-fuel vehicles. Here
items.text: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) has amended the Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR), 1989, to permit the use of ethanol concentrations of up to E100 in compatible flex-fuel vehicles (FFVs). The amendment, notified through a gazette notification, expands the existing framework that includes E85 and is aimed at encouraging the adoption of vehicles capable of running on higher ethanol blends. The move is part of India’s broader efforts to reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels, lower emissions and support the agricultural sector. Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari has also highlighted the potential benefits of ethanol blending for farmers. However, the latest notification does not, by itself, establish a transition plan for vehicles already on Indian roads that are designed to run on lower ethanol blends. E100 Approval Brings Existing Vehicle Compatibility into Focus Vehicles designed for ethanol blends above E20 require fuel system components and engine calibration suited to higher ethanol concentrations. Consequently, vehicles developed specifically for E20 fuel cannot be assumed to be compatible with E85 or E100. This distinction is important as India expands its ethanol fuel framework. While the latest amendment provides a regulatory pathway for compatible FFVs to use higher blends, questions remain about the long-term fuel options available to owners of vehicles designed for E20 or lower blends. items.title: Electric Two-Wheeler Purchase Intent Rises to 43%, Market Penetration at 9.9% Through August: BCG
items.summary: The share of consumers actively considering electric two-wheelers rose from 30% in 2024, while those rejecting the category declined to 29%, according to a BCG survey.
items.text: The share of consumers actively considering electric two-wheelers rose from 30% in 2024, while those rejecting the category declined to 29%, according to a BCG survey. The share of Indian consumers actively considering an electric two-wheeler as their next purchase rose to 43% in 2026 from 30% in 2024, even as electric vehicles accounted for less than 10% of overall two-wheeler sales in FY27 through August, according to a report by Boston Consulting Group (BCG). The report, titled Electric in Charge: How India's Electric Two-Wheelers Are Moving into the Mainstream, found that outright rejection of electric two-wheelers declined to 29% from 38% over the same period, reflecting growing consumer acceptance of the technology. While 43% of respondents said they were actively considering electric two-wheelers as part of their next purchase within six months, another 28% were open to the category but unlikely to adopt it in that period, compared with 32% in 2024. "The electric two-wheeler is no longer an experiment for early adopters. It is now a default consideration for a growing share of Indian buyers," said Natarajan Sankar, Managing Director and Senior Partner, BCG. The growing interest is also reflected in vehicle sales. According to BCG analysis, electric two-wheeler penetration increased to 9.9% in FY27 year-to-date through August 2026 from 5.5% in FY24. items.title: Quick-Commerce Boom Creates New Demand Segment for India’s Electric Two-Wheeler Makers: BCG
items.summary: Delivery riders travelling 400–500 km a week are emerging as a distinct customer group, with affordability, speed and manoeuvrability shaping vehicle preferences, according to a BCG report.
items.text: Delivery riders travelling 400–500 km a week are emerging as a distinct customer group, with affordability, speed and manoeuvrability shaping vehicle preferences, according to a BCG report. India’s rapid growth in quick commerce and food delivery is creating a new category of two-wheeler buyers, opening opportunities for electric vehicle manufacturers to develop products suited to high-frequency delivery operations, according to a Boston Consulting Group (BCG) report. The report, titled Electric in Charge: How India’s Electric Two-Wheelers Are Moving into the Mainstream , identifies a new consumer segment called “Trip Maximizers”, comprising full-time delivery riders working with quick-commerce and food-delivery platforms. These riders typically cover 400–500 km a week and prioritise affordability, speed and ease of manoeuvrability when choosing a two-wheeler. The emergence of this segment comes amid the rapid expansion of India’s quick-commerce industry, which grew from approximately $750 million in 2022 to $8 billion in 2025, representing a compound annual growth rate of around 120%, according to the BCG report. According to the survey, affordability is the most important consideration for 72% of riders in this segment, followed by speed at 55% and manoeuvrability at 50%. Around 66% use scooters, while 85% typically travel alone. The Bajaj Pulsar NS400Z and duke 390 (350cc) approach this segment differently, catering to riders with varying priorities and budgets. Although their engine specifications suggest that the two motorcycles deliver comparable performance, their hardware, equipment and overall character set them apart. Here's a closer look at how they compare and which one might be the better choice for you. The KTM 390 Duke commands a premium, but the Pulsar NS400Z's lower price makes it an appealing option for buyers who want a capable streetfighter without stretching their finances. The KTM 390 Duke has an 8mm longer wheelbase and 18mm more ground clearance than the Pulsar NS400Z. Its greater clearance could prove useful on uneven roads, while the longer wheelbase contributes to better stability. The Duke also gets a larger 15-litre fuel tank, compared to the Pulsar's 12-litre unit, giving it an advantage in terms of overall range. The Pulsar NS400Z's 805mm seat height makes it a relatively accessible option for a wider range of riders. This can be particularly useful when navigating traffic or manoeuvring the motorcycle at low speeds in the city. The KTM 390 Duke offers two seat-heights of 800mm and 820mm. events.text: Harley-Davidson is recalling motorcycles worldwide where the vent hole in the air filter box’s base plate may be blocked by plastic. This causes pressure to build up in the crankcase. If the dipstick is pulled out without allowing the pressure to escape slowly first, oil may spray out of the filler neck. The recall has the manufacturer code 0193. It is listed with the NHTSA as Campaign 26V270 and with Germany’s Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA) under reference number 16507R. One injury has been reported. As of October 6, 2026. U.S. figures from the NHTSA, figures for Germany and worldwide from the Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA). Harley-Davidson operates a public recall lookup service based on the VIN. No registration or customer account is required. It also recognizes German motorcycles; we tested this with the VIN of a Harley registered in Germany, and the system returned the active recall 0193. The search feature is only available on the U.S. Harley website; the German site does not offer this option. Your VIN is located on the steering head, on a sticker on the right front frame tube, and in field E of the vehicle registration certificate. The base plate of the air filter box, part number 29000373, has a vent through which gases are expelled from the crankcase. Due to a manufacturing defect at the supplier, plastic may block this passage. If the opening is sealed, the gases can no longer escape, and pressure builds up in the crankcase. events.text: Since its inception, KTM has always carried a reputation for loud graphics, sharp angles, and aggressive styling. Critics often dismiss the brand as style over substance. They argue that Austrian bikes sell purely on loud attitude. Yet, reducing the brand to bright bodywork misses the engineering beneath the surface. KTM built its global identity around uncompromising competition hardware and success in many racing disciplines. The brand’s "Ready to Race" motto is an actual development standard, not just a catchy slogan. Its new bikes are fitting proof of the same, as the bikemaker tries to put its financial woes in the past. A baby supermoto serves as the prime example. The idea that KTM relies on flashy bodywork falls apart the second you examine how these bikes are engineered. Many rival motorcycle brands take commuter frames, wrap them in modern fairings, and call it a day. KTM does the opposite. The company designs its motorcycles around high-performance chassis dynamics, premium suspension, and lightweight components. Over the past decade the domestic revenue of India’s listed auto makers has compounded at 11% a year, and the dealers who sell and service these vehicles have ridden that growth. We estimate that India’s auto dealers now earn about Rs 14,000 crore of net profit a year – more than double the FY16 level – and have earned roughly around Rs 1 lakh crore cumulatively over the decade. The average dealer makes around Rs 80 lakhs of PAT a year, 7x the income of an average middle-class taxpayer. A typical car dealer runs around 3 dealerships and makes about Rs 2.5 crore of PAT/yr.
